0|4af7715110a2617fc40ac2c1232f664019269f3a|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"KVM: x86/mmu: Add explicit access mask for MMIO SPTEs
When shadow paging is enabled
column2: KVM tracks the allowed access type for

column1: MMIO SPTEs so that it can do a permission check on a MMIO GVA cache hit
without having to walk the guest's page tables.  The tracking is done
by retaining the WRITE and USER bits of the access when inserting the
MMIO SPTE (read access is implicitly allowed)
page fault handler to retrieve and cache the WRITE/USER bits from the
SPTE.
Unfortunately for EPT
column2: the mask used to retain the WRITE/USER bits is

column1: hardcoded using the x86 paging versions of the bits.  This funkiness
happens to work because KVM uses a completely different mask/value for
MMIO SPTEs when EPT is enabled
column2: and the EPT mask/value just happens to

column1: overlap exactly with the x86 WRITE/USER bits[*].
Explicitly define the access mask for MMIO SPTEs to accurately reflect
that EPT does not want to incorporate any access bits into the SPTE
so that KVM isn't subtly relying on EPT's WX bits always being set in
MMIO SPTEs
column2: e.g. attempting to use other bits for experimentation breaks

column1: horribly.
Note
TDP flows explicit set mmio_gva to 0
EPT has no (known) functional impact.
[*] Using WX to generate EPT misconfigurations (equivalent to reserved
bit page fault) ensures KVM can employ its MMIO page fault tricks
even platforms without reserved address bits.
